task_instance: Build and validate a Store-ready MSIX for a minimal packaged full-trust Win32 app ('Hello Tray'): pack it with makeappx.exe, inspect its identity/publisher/display name/architecture/signing state with the skill's inspect-msix.ps1, and run the Windows App Certification Kit via invoke-wack.ps1 to confirm it passes. This is the concrete deliverable that must exist before any Partner Center submission, and it needs no account.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable requires Windows-only tooling that this Linux runtime does not provide and that cannot be installed on this platform. The MSIX build/inspection step needs makeappx.exe from the Windows 11 SDK, and the validation step needs the Windows App Certification Kit (appcert.exe); both skill scripts (inspect-msix.ps1, invoke-wack.ps1) are PowerShell and resolve tools under the Windows SDK install path and %LOCALAPPDATA%. The runtime is Linux x86_64 with no PowerShell, no makeappx.exe and no appcert.exe present, and these are Windows binaries that will not run on Linux. The final submission phase would additionally require a Microsoft Partner Center developer account with interactive Microsoft sign-in and would write to a production external service, which is separately barred by the safety rules.
